purpose: Forecast held-out unseen malicious behaviour from attack-free network histories using causal topology churn, edge persistence, fan-out and periodicity features in addition to traffic dynamics.
source: Official CTU IoT-23 timestamped Zeek conn.log.labeled scenarios
final_validation: locked; no final-validation family may be scored while V29 development is tuned

temporal_protocol.heldout_family_rule: all blocks with held-out-family history or future exposure are excluded from train/calibration/policy
temporal_protocol.test_positive: fully benign history followed by held-out family within 30-240 seconds
temporal_protocol.test_negative: fully benign history with fully benign next four minutes
temporal_protocol.split: deterministic one-hour block split inherited from V23

feature_policy.allowed_identity_use: IP/edge/port identities may only be used transiently to compute aggregate causal counts, overlap, churn, entropy and persistence; identities themselves never enter the model

model.supervised_future_head: balanced HistGradientBoostingClassifier trained on non-heldout clean histories
model.novelty_head: IsolationForest fitted on clean benign train histories only
model.selection: policy split only; maximize non-heldout future recall subject to <=2.05% policy benign FPR, then lower FPR and lower novelty weight

claim_boundary: A pass supports forecasting these held-out unseen development behaviours from clean network histories. It does not prove prediction of every zero-day attack.
